verses.author: model_A
verses.text: The train slows for a station no one gets off at.

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
Someone left a window cracked open in the empty house—
the curtains breathe for no one now.

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
A dog barks twice at nothing on the road,
then settles back to sleep in the warm dust.

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
The vending machine hums its one note
all night to the empty parking lot.

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
Someone's left umbrella spins slowly
in the coffee shop corner, waiting to be claimed—
rain long since stopped outside.

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
The bus schedule taped to the pole
has faded past reading—
still, someone stands there each morning.

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
A crow lands on the wire, shifts its weight,
lets one feather go to the wind—
doesn't watch it fall.

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
The kitchen clock loses a minute a day—
close enough, she says,
and pours the coffee anyway.

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
Someone's traced initials in the dust
on the windowsill, then wiped them clean
before the dust could settle on a name.

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
The neighbor's radio hums through the wall,
a song from before I was born—
I learn the chorus without meaning to.

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
Rain fills the boot left out by the door,
a small lake for the sparrows—
nobody thought to bring it in.

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
Half a loaf gone stale on the counter,
still I slice it thin,
butter what's left before it's gone.

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
The porch light burns on through the noon,
no one remembers who turned it on—
moths circle anyway, out of habit.

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
The kettle clicks off in an empty kitchen,
steam finding the cold window—
someone's name almost surfaces, then doesn't.

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
A dog barks twice at nothing down the road,
then settles back to sleep in the dust—
the gate was never latched anyway.

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
I keep the receipt from that day,
folded so long the ink's given up—
still I check my pocket for it.
